headline: A UK research network used AI to reject half of 179 grant proposals before any human read them, and the national funder says its rules forbid that.
score_reason: A real integrity row with a funder admission, but the episode was first reported on 27 Sep 2026 and Science's account is a late retelling, so one point below the pool score.
importance_line: Researchers who spent weeks on bids learned they were culled by machine scoring before human review, UK Research and Innovation now has to police its own networks on AI use, and the open question is whether the review will change how the surviving half were ranked.
summary: Times Higher Education reports that the CRANE cybersecurity pilot, a funding call hosted at the University of Oxford with money from UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), ran 179 proposals through several AI models scored on seven criteria and sent only the top half on to human reviewers; the episode was first reported on 27 Sep 2026 and Science has now published its own account. A UKRI spokesperson said its policy "does not allow the use of generative AI to conduct application assessment" and that it is reviewing the network's compliance, while UKRI is itself consulting on how to cope with an AI-driven flood of applications.
notes: Science article blocked (403); entry written from the full THE report of the same story, so the source and link are THE. The Science headline says 'U.K. funder'; THE shows the AI triage was run by the UKRI-funded CRANE network, not by UKRI itself, and UKRI says it breaches policy.
